subject.title: feat(self-host): local console sign-in without Cloudflare Access

question: Should the supported Docker self-host profile enable local admin-token browser sign-in by default on upgrade, rather than preserving the previous API-only fail-closed dashboard until an operator opts in?
rationale: This is a new privileged authentication and deployment-default policy, not a mechanical correctness choice; the earlier self-host work identified token-based console login only as a possible follow-up.

options.title: Enable by default with explicit upgrade documentation
options.body: Accept the new self-host default, provided the operator-visible upgrade posture and disabled escape hatch are documented and proven.

options.title: Require explicit opt-in
options.body: Keep existing self-host upgrades API-only unless an operator sets the local-auth flag, reducing unexpected new browser attack surface.

options.title: Defer the feature
options.body: Keep the current API-only self-host profile until maintainers choose a broader self-host authentication direction.

recommendation.title: Enable by default with explicit upgrade documentation
recommendation.body: Accept the new self-host default, provided the operator-visible upgrade posture and disabled escape hatch are documented and proven.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced the self-host profile and adjacent session-based administrative functionality that define the affected product boundary.
